subject: Computer Networking
title: GitHub's Database Failover (2018)
description: A quick, practical guide to GitHub's Database Failover (2018).

hook.text: On October 21, 2018, GitHub was degraded for over 24 hours. Developers worldwide lost access to code.

buildup.text: A 43-second network cut triggered a database failover that created two active primaries writing at once.

discovery.text: Both databases accepted writes independently. Merging them without data loss was extremely complex.

twist.text: GitHub chose data integrity over speed, spending hours to reconcile rather than risk losing any commits.

climax.text: Their transparent post-mortem earned industry respect. Exact timelines and decisions were shared openly.

punchline.text: 43 seconds of network loss caused 24 hours of recovery.

quiz.question: What caused GitHub's 2018 extended outage?
options: A brief network cut triggered a database split-brain with two primaries
A hacker deleted all code repositories
A fire destroyed GitHub's primary data center

details.summary: In October 2018, a 43-second network interruption triggered GitHub's MySQL database to fail over to a secondary. The secondary had fallen behind, creating data inconsistencies. GitHub chose data integrity over availability and spent 24 hours carefully reconciling before full restoration.
details.whyItMatters: GitHub's response demonstrated that sometimes the right choice is to stay offline longer to protect data integrity rather than rush back online with corrupt data.
takeaways: A 43-second blip triggered a database failover cascade
The secondary database had fallen behind the primary
GitHub prioritized data integrity over speed of recovery

faq.question: Why did a 43-second interruption cause a 24-hour outage?
faq.answer: The brief interruption triggered automatic failover to a secondary database that had replication lag. New writes went to the secondary while the primary had different data. Reconciling the two without data loss required careful, manual work that took 24 hours.

faq.question: What lesson does this teach about database failover?
faq.answer: Automatic failover can create worse problems if secondaries are not perfectly synchronized. Replication lag must be monitored continuously. GitHub's decision to prioritize correctness over speed protected millions of repositories from data corruption.
